note: PLACEHOLDER. Every params object here validates against the published top_community_issues manifest input_schema (additionalProperties: false, $refs inlined the way publish_experiments.py inlines them), and every value is plausible, but nobody has dispatched one. So a verdict drawn from this list is a claim about the pipeline, not about the agent. EIGHT cases, and DEFAULT_JUDGE_CONFIG.gates.minCases is 20. A corpus verdict over this list therefore resolves CAN'T SAY however the judge voted, because the floor was set from measured agent non-determinism and eight runs measure that rather than the branch. Eight is deliberate and not a rounding error: one clean baseline plus seven single-axis variations is what one change can author honestly. Whether to grow every list to 20 or to lower the floor is still open — do not read the shortfall as a decision. {judgeOrgSlug} is not a value: they are substituted at dispatch time from the per-sweep test fixture in sweepFixture.ts, and assertNoPlaceholders refuses the whole list before the first dispatch if a sweep did not supply one. A literal slug cannot be written here, because the only supported way to get a dev organization in a known state is POST /v1/test-fixtures/users and those users are swept after about 24 hours — so a hardcoded one is right for a day and then makes every later sweep read as an agent failure. The organization is therefore the one axis this list cannot vary, and here it is load-bearing rather than decorative: step 2 reads the current issue feed with GET_community_issues scoped to this slug so carried issues keep their existing IDs, which is a real lookup against a real elected office. The fixture's org is a fresh one, so that read returns an empty feed on both arms — the instruction's documented 404 branch, identical for base and candidate, which is the property a comparison needs even though it leaves the carry-forward path unexercised. Varied along: district geometry, which is what decides whether the L2 predicate is a ward string, a bare district number or a whole jurisdiction — City_Ward, City_Council_Commissioner_District, City, County_Commissioner_District and Borough_Ward each appear; district population, where a Minneapolis ward and a Bellefonte borough ward are two orders of magnitude of voter file rows and of how much local news exists to attach to a ranked issue; urban against rural; and one case with no L2 pair at all, which is the documented fallback to state scope and the only way the lean annotation's absence gets exercised. People are fictional placeholders in the house style (gp-webapp e2e-tests briefings.spec.ts uses 'Test Official'); this file is public, so no real person is named and every URL is under example.org. States, cities, office titles and L2 voter file column names are real. THE ORG SLUG IS AN ECHO, NOT A LOOKUP, and the geography is carried by the other params. {judgeOrgSlug} resolves to the sweep fixture's Cheyenne, WY elected office for every case, while each case's own state/office/district_descriptor names somewhere else. That is not a mismatch to fix in this file: under the judge harness the dispatch message's organization_slug is pinned to judge-* (see JUDGE_ORG_SLUG_PREFIX in runners/background.ts), and that pin — not this param — is what scopes any gp-api read the agent makes, so no lookup resolves against the value here. Both arms receive the identical value, so the comparison is unaffected. Whether these three agents should get a fixture whose geography matches their cases is an open question recorded on the PR.
